author: blu
body: The acknowledgement a QoS 1 PUBLISH is answered with, and the one a subscriber must send for a QoS 1 delivery it receives. Neither direction could be expressed before: the packet type was in the enumeration and no builder produced it, so a client that subscribed at QoS 1 took delivery and never acknowledged, and the broker redelivered forever.

author: blu
body: A packet, split into its fixed header and everything after it. `mp-total` is what the caller must drop from its buffer -- TCP delivers a byte stream and a segment can carry half a packet or three, so a reader that does not know how much it consumed cannot find the next one.

author: blu
body: PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL and PUBCOMP all carry the same body -- a packet identifier and an optional reason -- so one reader serves all four. The neutral name exists because a caller reading a PUBCOMP through something called `puback-id` is a sentence that invites the wrong packet.
